title: Fix the flaky Tunnel busy-slot test and the lost 503
body:
The Tunnel test control::tunnel::tests::stalled_callers_without_a_token_free_their_slots_at_the_head_deadline (src/control/tunnel.rs, added by commit 03761b2) is flaky: it failed 4 of 13 runs on this PC, panicking at the assert that a non-200 reply starts with "HTTP/1.1 503 " with an EMPTY reply string. Reproduce with: cargo test --target-dir target/agent stalled_callers_without_a_token (run it ten times).
Likely cause, to confirm before fixing: on the busy path the listener writes 503 and closes the socket while the request bytes the client already sent are still unread in the receive buffer. On Windows closing a socket with unread data sends a reset, so the client can lose the 503 and see a reset instead. That is a product bug as well as a test bug: a real curl caller would get "connection reset" instead of 503. The other refusal paths already linger; check every early-refusal path (busy, 401, 413, 501, 400) for the same thing.
Fix the cause in the listener (for example shut down the write half and drain or linger briefly, bounded by a deadline, before closing), not by loosening the test. Do not add a crate. Do not change routes or the pipe protocol.
Blocked by: Harden the Tunnel listener and send the reply note at launch
Done when:
- the root cause is stated in the commit body with what was observed
- the test passes 30 runs in a row (run it in a loop and report the count)
- a caller refused as busy after it has already sent its request reliably reads the 503 (test)
- the drain or linger is bounded so a refused caller cannot hold a thread past the head deadline
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent control; cargo test --target-dir target/agent chat
